_about: Starter fault knowledge base for the FixSaathi MVP. General field-repair knowledge plus notes from Jitendra (AC and appliance technician, Mumbai). Every guided repair adds verified entries over time.
safety_rules: Switch off the appliance AND the MCB / main for that circuit before opening any cover.
In old homes the wiring may be reversed (switch on neutral), so the line can stay live even when the switch is off. Always confirm with a line tester before touching wires. (Jitendra)
Discharge capacitors (fan, AC compressor/fan, washing machine motor) before touching their terminals.
Use insulated tools, dry hands and dry footwear. Never work standing on a wet floor.
For ACs: never open the refrigerant circuit without gauges and recovery equipment; gas work only by a certified technician.
If there is burning smell, melted insulation or water near live parts, isolate power and escalate.

faults.symptom: fan runs slow / speed low / humming

causes.check: Visually check for bulging or leakage; measure with a capacitance meter or swap with a known-good capacitor of the same rating.
Bypass the regulator (connect fan directly) and see if speed becomes normal.
With power off, spin the blades by hand; rough or tight rotation means bearing issue.
Measure voltage at the ceiling rose.

causes.cause: No supply at the fan: loose connection, failed switch or regulator
causes.check: Use a line tester at the canopy connector and at the switch board.
If fan hums but does not start, or starts when pushed by hand, the capacitor is likely dead.
Check winding continuity with a multimeter; burnt smell confirms.
Tighten canopy screws and down-rod bolt, check split pin.
Measure blade tip heights; replace a bent blade.

causes.cause: Dirty air filter or indoor coil
causes.check: Open the front panel; inspect and clean the filters; check coil for dust.

causes.cause: Outdoor unit fan not running or condenser coil blocked
causes.check: Check whether the outdoor fan spins when the compressor runs; look for blocked or dirty fins.

causes.cause: Weak capacitor on the outdoor unit (compressor or fan)
causes.check: Look for a bulging capacitor; measure capacitance.
Oil marks at flare joints, frost on the service valve. Pressure check by a certified technician only.
Confirm Cool mode, 24 C, fan speed auto.
Pour water in the drain tray and see if it flows out; clear the pipe.
Check with a spirit level; drain side must be slightly lower.

causes.cause: No supply / tripped MCB / loose plug
causes.check: Check the MCB and socket with a tester.
Use the manual button on the indoor unit.
Check the PCB fuse; look for burnt marks. Escalate if PCB replacement is needed.

causes.cause: Overload: too many appliances on one circuit
causes.check: Note which appliances run when it trips; compare load with MCB rating.

causes.cause: Short circuit in an appliance or wiring
causes.check: Switch off all loads, reset, then switch on one load at a time to find the culprit.
Check appliances with metal bodies and wet areas (geyser, washing machine).
If it trips with very low load, replace the MCB of the same rating.
Front load: open the drain filter at the bottom front with a cloth and tray. Top load: check the drain hose for kinks or lint.
Listen for the pump hum during drain; check for a foreign object at the impeller.
Redistribute clothes and run spin again.

causes.cause: Transit bolts not removed (new front load)
causes.check: Check the back panel for transit bolts.
Check belt tension (top load); escalate for motor or PCB.

causes.cause: Dirty condenser coil or poor ventilation
causes.check: Check the back or bottom coil for dust; keep 10 cm space behind the fridge.
Close the door on a paper strip; if it slides out easily, the gasket is weak.
Compressor clicks on and off without running suggests relay/OLP. Escalate for compressor or gas.
